slides.title: Rough [[hands]] this season?
slides.photo_prompt: Photorealistic lifestyle photo, vertical 4:5. Close-up of a Korean woman's hands at a bright bathroom sink on a winter morning, gently patting her hands dry with a soft white towel, a plain unbranded hand cream tube and a bar of soap on the counter beside her, faint steam on the window behind, face out of frame. Mint green and cream color palette, soft natural light, clean minimal set, shallow depth of field, editorial beauty magazine style. slides.title: Sound like [[you]]?
items: Hand cream seems gone in an hour

slides.title: Lots of [[washing]]
slides.body: Frequent washing, especially with hot water, rinses away the natural oils on your hands. With less oil, moisture slips away faster.
slides.speech: Hot water is the sneaky one!

slides.title: Cold, [[dry]] air
slides.body: Cold outdoor air and indoor heating are both low in humidity. Your hands are usually uncovered, so they meet that dry air all day.

items.head: Use lukewarm water
items.sub: Skip hot water when you wash

items.head: Pat dry, then moisturize
items.sub: Hand cream within a few minutes

items.head: Wear gloves outside
items.sub: Cover up on cold, windy days

slides.title: Hand care [[checklist]]
slides.note: Lifestyle tips only. If it lasts, talk to a professional.

slides.title: Soft hands with [[Clear]]!
slides.body: Save, share and tell a friend

caption:
Rough hands this season? 🧼

Frequent washing with hot water rinses away your hands' natural oils, and cold air plus indoor heating keep things dry all day.
Try three small habits starting tonight:
Use lukewarm water · Pat dry, then moisturize · Wear gloves outside
